text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- It was logical for the Bulgarian lev to rise against the dollar because it had been seriously undervalued recently, the Bulgarian National Bank governor Lyubomir Filipov said.

-- Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftochim said it had lifted the limits on fuel distribution to local retailers although the refinery is still processing only 9,000 tonnes of crude per day, down from 22,000 tonnes per day in December. @

-- Bulgaria's interim energy minister Georgi Stoilov said that safety at the country's Kozloduy nuclear power plant is not meeting socially acceptable risk standards despite improvements at the plant in recent years.
-- The privatisation of Bulgaria's chemical fertiliser producer Chimko is expected to be finalised by the end of April, Chimko's executive director Kiril Petkov said.
-- Bulgaria needs around $70 million for fertilisers and pesticides to secure this year grain crop, the Bulgarian Agricultural Chamber said.
-- Bulgaria's interim cabinet is expected to discuss today a possible rise of electricity and coal prices and a liberalisation of central heating prices.

-- The sale of a 60 percent stake in the Bulgarian soda ash producer Sodi-Devnya to the Belgian chemical company Solvay SA is expected to be finalised by end-February, Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency executive director Vesselin Blagoev said.
-- Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet is expected on Monday to raise the minimum monthly salary in the public sector to 22,000 levs from 11,000 levs, trade union officials said. @

-- Bulgaria's state-owned Bulbank (formerly Bulgarian Foreign Trade Bank) is in talks for buying a 34 percent stake in the Central Co-operative Bank (CCB), Balkan news agency said, quoting CCB sources.

-- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is ready to invest some $100-200 million in Bulgaria once the caretaker cabinet has an agreement with the International Monetary Fund, EBRD resident representative Tim O'Neill said.

-- Bulgaria's Agriculture ministry has issued permission to five foreign companies to import a total of 150,000 tonnes of wheat to Bulgaria under a pledge to export the same volume from this year's crop, the newspaper said without quoting sources. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
